steps.reason: Data pack syntax, pack formats, command trees, and vanilla data paths are version-specific.
evidence: Target Java version is explicit or resolved from the bundled latest alias.
The selected version has extracted pack format and data pack coverage.
steps.failureMode: Do not copy pack_format or version-specific syntax from memory when the target version is unresolved.

steps.reason: minecraft-skills surfaces distinguish observed facts from normative specifications.
evidence: Relevant datapack fact surfaces were inspected for guarantees and non-guarantees.
Observed schema data is treated as observed vanilla data, not a complete JSON schema.
steps.failureMode: Do not claim a generated JSON shape is valid for all packs when only observed vanilla examples are available.

steps.reason: Commands and vanilla data paths can be checked against extracted official server data.
evidence: Command literals, arguments, or parsers used in output were searched for the target version.
Vanilla data paths referenced by output were searched for the target version.
steps.failureMode: If a command or path is not found, describe it as unverified instead of presenting it as a version fact.

steps.reason: Observed vanilla datapack JSON fields help avoid invented field names while preserving the observed-only boundary.
evidence: Observed field paths were checked for the relevant datapack kind when JSON fields are version-sensitive.
Downloadable schema surface data was fetched when the target surface was not bundled locally.
steps.failureMode: If no observed surface exists for the target version, state the gap and use versioned sources instead of fabricating fields.

steps.reason: Resource pack formats, vanilla asset paths, model shapes, and item definitions are version-specific.
evidence: Target Java version is explicit or resolved from the bundled latest alias.
The selected version has extracted resource pack format and asset coverage.
steps.failureMode: Do not reuse a pack_format or item model convention from another version without checking the target version.

steps.reason: Resource pack model summaries are extracted from vanilla assets and are not normative schemas.
evidence: Resource pack fact surfaces were inspected for guarantees and non-guarantees.
Model summary data is treated as observed vanilla data.
steps.failureMode: Do not claim a model JSON structure is complete or plugin-defined when only vanilla observations are available.

steps.reason: Vanilla asset inventories and model summaries reduce invented namespaces, paths, and item definition fields.
evidence: Referenced vanilla asset paths were searched for the target version.
Model or item definition fields were checked against extracted vanilla model summaries when relevant.
steps.failureMode: If a path or model field is not found, mark it as custom or unverified rather than vanilla.

steps.reason: Paper support can lag the latest Java release, and plugin API references are tied to supported Minecraft versions.
evidence: The target Minecraft version is listed as Paper-supported or the gap is explicitly stated.
The versioned Paper API dependency and Javadocs URL are resolved for supported versions.
steps.failureMode: Do not generate a Paper dependency for an unsupported latest Java version unless the support gap is stated.

steps.reason: Javadocs package/type/member indexes prove names and labels, not behavior, nullability, or thread safety.
evidence: Paper API fact surfaces were inspected for guarantees and non-guarantees.
Type/member search results are treated as API surface facts only.
steps.failureMode: Do not infer method behavior, overload semantics, or Folia safety from a type/member label alone.

steps.reason: Paper Javadocs indexes and event search reduce hallucinated class names, methods, and event candidates.
evidence: Referenced Paper/Bukkit types and members were searched for the target Paper version.
Events discovered by behavior or partial name are treated as candidates until checked against Paper/Bukkit docs.
steps.failureMode: If a type, member, or event is not found, do not invent an API; state that the surface did not verify it.

steps.reason: Threading and scheduler behavior is behavior documentation, not derivable from API surface indexes alone.
evidence: Scheduler and Folia documentation links from the Paper API reference were considered for code touching worlds, entities, chunks, or async work.
steps.failureMode: Do not silently use global scheduler patterns for Folia-sensitive work without noting the assumption.
